narr: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
ev: A significant flash flood wave in Pine Creek was reported by Zion National Park staff.

The Iron County Emergency Manager reported six feet of water flowed over a flood control barrier in Paragonah, resulting in flash flooding in the city. Several homes were flooded. Fifty people were stranded in Red Creek Canyon east of the city.
Water flowed across many roadways in Cedar City, including across Interstate 15 near milepost 59.
A video showed flash flooding at the confluence of Birch and North Creeks into the Escalante River.
The Escalante River gauge near Escalante indicated a rise from 3 CFS to 1060 CFS, a rise of 4 feet.
Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument officials reported that significant damage was sustained on House Rock Road near Wire Pass due to flash flooding.
A received video showed a flood wave with significant debris moving through Big Water, UT.
The Paria - Kanab gauge on the Paria River indicated a rise from 23 CFS to 1450 CFS with the primary flood wave. The time above 1000 CFS was from 2315 MDT to 0130 MDT.

Video received showed significant flows through a normally dry wash just south of Tropic, including a mature fully grown tree floating beneath an underpass along Bryce Highway. In addition, Bryce Canyon National Park officials reported the closure of the Queens Garden Trail, Navajo Loop, and the road to Bryce Point due to flooding.
Video received showed 2 to 3 feet deep water flowing down a street in Hildale, eroding a portion of the road.
Zion National Park officials reported flash flooding in portions of the park, including the Narrows, Kolob Canyons, and Telephone Canyon.
The manager of Veyo Pool Resort reported a 7 foot rise on the Santa Clara River. Campsites were evacuated near the river.

Capitol Reef National Park officials reported flash flooding across Scenic Drive in multiple locations, including Grand Wash and across State Route 24, closing the road. A muddy debris flow was also reported in Sulphur Creek.
The Iron County Emergency Manager reported flooding in Parowan. Floodwaters moved protective concrete barriers for the power plant and pushed them into the power plant building.

Video received showed deep and swift moving water flowing westward down Center Street and 700 E in Paragonah. Flows originated from Red Creek, which empties into Paragonah from the east. Radar estimated up to 2.15 inches of rain upstream over the Red Creek drainage.
